texts.orig: Under the Romans the district was included in the province of   Belgica prima, afterwards   forming part  of the Frankish kingdom of Austrasia and ỏf the empire of Charlemagne. About Io6o it came under the rule of Conrad (d. 1086), who took the title of count of Luxemburg: His descendants ruled the county, frst in the male and then in the female until the death of the   emperor   Sigismund in 1437. Through the marriage  of the house of Habsburg; but was seized in 1443 by Philip IIL the Good, duke of Burgundy, who based his claim upon a bargain concluded with Sigismund's niece Elizabeth (d. 1451)Regained by the Habsburgs in 1477 when Mary, daughter and heiress of duke Charles the Bold, married the German king Maximilian L , the duchy passed to Philip II. of Spain in 1555, though subject to the laws of the empire, of which ỉt still formed part. After section had been ceded to France in 1659, the remainder was given to the emperor Charles VI by the treaty of Utrecht in 1713. It was conquered by France in 1795, and retained by that power until the end of the Napoleonic wars. The congress of Vienna (1814-1815) erected Luxemburg into a grand-duchy, added part of the duchy of Bouillon to ỉt, and assigned ỉt to William 1, king of the Netherlands, in return for the German territories of the bouse of Orange-Nassau, which Napoleon had Line, confiscated in 1806, and which were given by the congress to the of Prussia. In 1830 when the Belgian provinces separated from Holland, an efort was made to include Luxemburg in the new kingdom of the Belgians; but in November 1831 the powers the of Holland, who refused to accept this arrangement_ Conscquently the whole of Luxemburg remained in the possession concluded at the conference of London, enforced the partition of 1831. king king By modifications of the treaty of Vienna the garrisoning of the fortress   of Luxemburg had passed into  Prussian   hands, an arrangement which lasted until 1867. In the previous year the German Confederation, to which the grand-duchy of Luxemhad belonged since 1815, had been dissolved; but the was not included in the new North German   Confederation, while King William III. proposed to sell his rights over the grand-duchy to France. The Prussians were irritated by this proposal, but war was averted, and the question was referred to a conference of the powers in London. The treaty of London, signed on the Ith of May 1867, decided that the Prussian garrison must be withdrawu and the fortress dismantled, which was done in 1872' At the same time the great powers guaranteed the neutrality of the ~duchy, and although member of the German Zollverein, Luxemburg now forms a sovereign and independent state. burg grand The grand-duchy of Luxemburg, the portion under the rule of   William L retaining the name; was ruled by the of Holland until the death of William IIL in 189. William's daughter;   Wilhelmina, succeeded to Holland but under the Salic law' the grand-duchy passed to his kinsman; Adolphus, duke of Nassau, who died in 1905, and was succeeded by his son William (b. 1852). kings The GRAND-Ducnx lies S.E. of Belgium. Its area is 999 sq. m , with The people are ncarly all Catholics. The country is rich ỉn iron ore. The hills in the south of the duchy are a continuation of the Lorraine plateau, and the northern districts are crossed in all directions by out runners from the Ardennes. streams mostly join the Moselle, which forms the boundary between Luxemburg and the Rhine province for about 20 m. The Sure or Sauer, the most important stream in the duchy, nses at Luxemburg; crosses the duchy, and forms the eastern boundary from the confluence of the Our till it joins the Moselle after course   of 50 during   which it receives the Wiltz,  Attert Alzette, White and Black Ernz, &c. The soil of Luxem generally good; the southern districts are on the whole the most fertile as well as the most populous. materials of all sorts are obtained   throughout the duchy. Besides   the iron furnaces, situated in the south near the Lorraine plateau, there are tanneries,   weaving and glove-making factories, paper-mills for all sorts of paper, breweries and distilleries; andsugar refinerics A German patois mixed wỉth Frealch words ỉs spoken throughout the country; but French, which is employed by the commercial community, is also the common speech on the French and Belgian frontiers Though líberty of worship prevails, Roman Catholicism is almost the sole form. The government is in the hands o the grand-duke, who sanctions and promulgates the laws. There is a council (staalsral) of 15 members. There is a chamber of deputies wỉth 48 members   elected by the cantons (12 in number) for six years, half the body being elected three years. No law can be passed without the consent of the chamber. Bills are introduced by house has also the right of initiative. A single battalion (150) of volunteers composes the grand-ducal army. The gendarmerie consists of about I50 men.
